public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 51

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/51](https://www.erdosproblems.com/51)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Nat

namespace Erdos51

/--
Is there an infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $a \in A$,
there is an integer n such that $\phi(n)=a$, and
yet if $n_a$ is the smallest such integer, then $\frac{n_a}{a} → \infty$ as $a → ∞$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_51 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, ∃ n : A → ℕ,
      A.Infinite ∧
      (∀ a : A, IsLeast (φ ⁻¹' {(a : ℕ)}) (n a)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun a : A => (n a : ℝ) / (a : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/-
The remarks from the erdosproblems site are the same as those in
[erdosproblems.com/694](https://www.erdosproblems.com/694).
-/

end Erdos51

reformulations.difference: The limit along A is expressed using atTop on the subtype A with its inherited order. Lean also permits zero in A and uses the totalized values φ(0) = 0 and 0 / 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An infinite subset A of ℕ is unbounded. Consequently, its subtype atTop equals the pullback of the ambient natural-number atTop and is nontrivial. The stated Tendsto condition is therefore equivalent to: for every real R, there exists N such that R ≤ n_a/a for every a ∈ A with N ≤ a. Zero causes no change to the existence question: removing it preserves infinitude and the limit. For positive a, every totient preimage is positive, so least preimages over ℕ agree with least positive preimages. The threshold equivalence and equivalence with the positive-element-restricted existential statement were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
